punchline: Doing the wrong thing on time and on budget is still doing the wrong thing.
thirty_sec: At IMVU, Eric Ries and his co-founders spent months building an IM add-on with 3D avatars that plugged into existing chat networks. They shipped it and almost nobody cared. When they talked to users, they found customers didn't want an add-on at all, so much of the work was thrown away. That lesson became The Lean Startup: ship a small version early, measure real behavior, learn, then decide whether to pivot or persevere.
question: When did you last let a real customer see your work before it was finished?
